units.zh: 嗚呼甚哉！
units.en: Alas—how extreme!
units.literal: Alas, how extreme!

units.zh: 自開平訖於顯德，終始五十三年，而天下五代。
units.en: From Kaiping to Xiande, fifty-three years passed—and through them the realm saw five dynasties.
units.literal: From the Kaiping era through Xiande, fifty-three years in all—and through that span the realm knew five dynasties.

units.zh: 士之不幸而生其時，欲全其節而不二者，固鮮矣。
units.en: Few were the scholars born into that age who could keep their integrity intact and never serve a second lord.
units.literal: Scholars unlucky enough to be born in that age who wished to keep their integrity whole and serve no second master were indeed few.

units.zh: 於此之時，責士以死與必去，則天下為無士矣。
units.en: In such an age, demanding that every gentleman die or quit office would have left the realm without gentlemen at all.
units.literal: At such a time, if one demanded that every gentleman die or certainly depart, the realm would have had no gentlemen left.

units.zh: 然其習俗，遂以茍生不去為當然。
units.en: Yet custom came to treat clinging to life and never leaving office as only natural.
units.literal: Yet custom came to treat clinging to life and not leaving as the natural thing.

units.zh: 至於儒者，以仁義忠信為學，享人之祿，任人之國者，不顧其存亡，皆恬然以茍生為得，非徒不知愧，而反以其得為榮者，可勝數哉！
units.en: Confucians trained in benevolence, righteousness, loyalty, and faith—men who ate another’s salary and governed another’s state—often ignored their state’s survival, calmly treating shameful survival as success; not only unashamed, they took it as glory. Their number was beyond counting!
units.literal: As for Confucians, who took benevolence, righteousness, loyalty, and faith as their study—men who enjoyed others’ salaries and bore charge of others’ states—many ignored whether those states lived or died, all calmly taking a shameful survival as gain; not only did they feel no shame, but took that gain as glory. Who could count them!

units.zh: 故吾於死事之臣，有所取焉。
units.en: That is why I find something worth honoring in ministers who died for their lord’s cause.
units.literal: Therefore in ministers who died for their lords’ cause I find something worth taking.

units.zh: 君子之於人也，樂成其美而不求其備，況死者人之所難乎？
units.en: A gentleman delights in another’s virtues and does not demand perfection—especially when death is what men find hardest.
units.literal: The gentleman toward others delights in completing their excellence and does not demand their perfection—how much more when death is what men find hardest?

units.zh: 吾於五代，得全節之士三人而已。
units.en: In the Five Dynasties I find only three men who kept their integrity intact throughout.
units.literal: In the Five Dynasties I find only three men who kept their integrity whole.

units.zh: 其初無卓然之節，而終以死人之事者，得十有五人焉，而戰沒者不得與也。
units.en: Fifteen men lacked outstanding integrity at first yet died for another’s cause in the end; those killed in battle are not counted here.
units.literal: Those who at first lacked outstanding integrity but in the end died for another’s cause number fifteen; those who died in battle are not counted among them.

units.zh: 然吾取王清、史彥超者，其有旨哉！
units.en: Yet that I include Wang Qing and Shi Yanchao—was there not a reason?
units.literal: Yet that I take Wang Qing and Shi Yanchao—was there not a point to it?

units.zh: 其有旨哉！
units.en: There was a reason!
units.literal: Was there not a point to it!

units.zh: 作《死事傳》。
units.en: Hence I wrote the “Biographies of Martyrs to Service.”
units.literal: I composed the “Biographies of Martyrs to Service.”

units.zh: 不能立傳者五人：馬彥超附朱守殷傳，宋令詢、李遐、張彥卿、鄭昭業見於本紀而已。
units.en: Five men could not receive full biographies: Ma Yanchao is appended to Zhu Shouyin’s biography; Song Lingxun, Li Xia, Zhang Yanqing, and Zheng Zhaoye appear only in the annals.
units.literal: Five men could not receive full biographies: Ma Yanchao is appended to the biography of Zhu Shouyin; Song Lingxun, Li Xia, Zhang Yanqing, and Zheng Zhaoye appear only in the basic annals.

units.zh: 張源德
units.en: Zhang Yuande
units.literal: Zhang Yuande

units.zh: 張源德者，不知其世家，或曰本晉人也。
units.en: Zhang Yuande’s lineage is unknown; some say he was originally from Jin.
units.literal: Zhang Yuande—his lineage is unknown; some say he was originally a man of Jin.

units.zh: 少事晉，無所稱。
units.en: In youth he served Jin without distinction.
units.literal: In youth he served Jin, with nothing to his credit.

units.zh: 從李罕之以潞州叛晉降梁，罕之遣源德見梁太祖。
units.en: He followed Li Hanzhi when Hanzhi rebelled at Luzhou and surrendered to Liang; Hanzhi sent Yuande to Emperor Taizu of Liang.
units.literal: He followed Li Hanzhi when Hanzhi rebelled against Jin at Luzhou and submitted to Liang; Hanzhi sent Yuande to see Emperor Taizu of Liang.

units.zh: 太祖時，源德自金吾衛將軍為蔡州刺史。
units.en: Under Taizu, Yuande rose from General of the Imperial Insignia Guard to prefect of Cai.
units.literal: Under Taizu, Yuande rose from General of the Imperial Insignia Guard to prefect of Cai.

units.zh: 梁貞明三年，魏博節度使楊師厚卒，末帝分魏、相等六州為兩鎮，懼魏軍不從，乃遣劉鄩將兵萬人，屯於魏以虞變。
units.en: In Liang’s third Zhenming year, Weibo governor Yang Shihou died; the Last Emperor split Wei and five other prefectures into two commands, fearing mutiny, and sent Liu Yan with ten thousand men to camp at Wei.
units.literal: In the third year of Zhenming of Liang, Yang Shihou, military governor of Weibo, died; the Last Emperor split the six prefectures of Wei and Xiang into two commands, fearing the Wei army would not obey, and sent Liu Yan with ten thousand men to camp at Wei to guard against trouble.

units.zh: 魏軍果叛，迫其節度使賀德倫以魏、博二州降晉。
units.en: The Wei army rebelled, forcing Governor He Delun to surrender Wei and Bo to Jin.
units.literal: The Wei army did rebel, forcing their governor He Delun to surrender Wei and Bo to Jin.

units.zh: 當是時，源德為鄩守貝州。
units.en: At that time Yuande, under Liu Yan, held Bei Prefecture.
units.literal: At that time Yuande was Liu Yan’s deputy defending Bei Prefecture.

units.zh: 晉王入魏，諸將欲先擊貝州，晉王曰：「貝城小而堅，攻之難卒下。
units.en: When the Prince of Jin entered Wei, his generals wanted to attack Bei first; he said, “Bei is small but strong—hard to seize quickly.
units.literal: When the Prince of Jin entered Wei, the generals wished to strike Bei first; the Prince of Jin said, “Bei’s walls are small but strong—hard to take at once.

units.zh: 且源德雖恃劉鄩之兵，然與滄州相首尾，今德州居其中而無備，不如先取之，則滄、貝之勢分而易圖也。」
units.en: Yuande relies on Liu Yan, but he and Cangzhou back each other; Dezhou lies between, undefended—take it first, and Cang and Bei will be split and easier to crack."
units.literal: Though Yuande relies on Liu Yan’s troops, he and Cangzhou support each other; Dezhou lies between them unguarded—better take it first, then Cang and Bei will be divided and easier to deal with."

units.zh: 乃先襲破德州，然後以兵五千攻源德，源德堅守不下，晉軍塹而圍之。
units.en: They stormed Dezhou first, then attacked Yuande with five thousand men; he held out, and the Jin army trenched and besieged him.
units.literal: They first stormed and took Dezhou, then attacked Yuande with five thousand men; Yuande held firm and would not yield, and the Jin army dug trenches and besieged him.

units.zh: 已而劉鄩大敗於故元城，南走黎陽，晉軍攻破洺州，而衛州刺史來昭、邢州節度使閻寶皆以城降晉，磁州刺史靳昭、相州張筠、滄州戴思遠皆棄城走。
units.en: Soon Liu Yan was crushed at Old Yuancheng and fled to Liyang; Jin took Luozhou; Lai Zhao of Weizhou and Yan Bao of Xingzhou surrendered; Jin Zhao, Zhang Yun, and Dai Siyuan fled their posts.
units.literal: Before long Liu Yan was routed at Old Yuancheng and fled south to Liyang; the Jin army took Luozhou, while Lai Zhao of Weizhou and Yan Bao of Xingzhou both surrendered their cities to Jin; Jin Zhao of Cizhou, Zhang Yun of Xiangzhou, and Dai Siyuan of Cangzhou all abandoned their posts and fled.

units.zh: 當此時，晉已先下全燕，而鎮、定皆附於晉，自河以北、山以東，四面千里，六鎮數十州之地皆歸晉，獨貝一州，圍之逾年不可下。
units.en: Jin had taken all Yan; Zhen and Ding submitted; for a thousand li north of the river and east of the mountains, six commands and dozens of prefectures fell to Jin—only Bei remained, besieged over a year without falling.
units.literal: By then Jin had already taken all of Yan; Zhen and Ding both submitted; north of the Yellow River and east of the mountains, a thousand li on four sides—the lands of six commands and dozens of prefectures—all went to Jin; Bei alone was besieged more than a year and could not be taken.

units.zh: 源德守既堅，而貝人聞晉已盡有河北，城中食且盡，乃勸源德出降，源德不從，遂見殺。
units.en: Yuande held firm, but Bei’s people heard Jin held all Hebei; food ran low; they urged surrender; he refused and was killed.
units.literal: Yuande’s defense was staunch, but the people of Bei heard Jin already held all Hebei; food in the city was nearly gone; they urged Yuande to surrender; he refused and was killed.

units.zh: 源德已死，貝人謀曰：「晉圍吾久，吾窮而後降，懼皆不免也。」
units.en: After Yuande’s death, Bei’s people said, “Jin has besieged us long—if we yield only when broken, none of us will be spared."
units.literal: After Yuande died, the people of Bei plotted: “Jin has besieged us long; if we surrender only when exhausted, we fear none will be spared."

units.zh: 乃告於晉曰：「吾欲被甲執兵而降，得赦而後釋之，如何？」
units.en: They asked Jin, “Let us surrender in armor, weapons in hand—grant amnesty, then we disarm. Will you?”
units.literal: They told Jin, “We wish to surrender in armor with weapons in hand—grant amnesty, then we will lay them down. How about it?”

units.zh: 晉軍許諾，貝人三千出降，已釋甲，晉兵四面圍而盡殺之。
units.en: Jin agreed; three thousand men of Bei surrendered and disarmed; Jin surrounded them and killed them all.
units.literal: The Jin army agreed; three thousand men of Bei came out to surrender; once they had laid down their arms, Jin troops surrounded them on four sides and slaughtered them all.

units.zh: 夏魯奇
units.en: Xia Luqi
units.literal: Xia Luqi

units.zh: 夏魯奇，字邦傑，青州人也。
units.en: Xia Luqi, courtesy name Bangjie, was from Qingzhou.
units.literal: Xia Luqi, courtesy name Bangjie, was a man of Qingzhou.

units.zh: 唐莊宗時，賜姓名曰李紹奇，其後莊宗賜姓名者，皆復其故。
units.en: Zhuangzong granted him the surname Li and the name Shaoqi; later all such granted names were restored.
units.literal: Under Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang he was granted the surname Li and the name Shaoqi; afterward all whom Zhuangzong had given surnames reverted to their former ones.

units.zh: 魯奇初事梁為宣武軍校，後奔於晉，為衛護指揮使。
units.en: Luqi first served Liang in the Xuanwu Army, then fled to Jin as commander of the Palace Guard.
units.literal: Luqi first served Liang as an officer of the Xuanwu Army, then fled to Jin and became commander of the Palace Guard.

units.zh: 從周德威攻劉守光於幽州，守光將單廷珪、元行欽以驍勇自負，魯奇每與二將鬥，輒不能解，兩軍皆釋兵而觀之。
units.en: With Zhou Dewei he besieged Liu Shouguang at Youzhou; Shouguang’s generals Shan Tinggui and Yuan Xingqin boasted of valor; Luqi duelled each in turn without decision, both armies watching.
units.literal: Following Zhou Dewei he attacked Liu Shouguang at Youzhou; Shouguang’s generals Shan Tinggui and Yuan Xingqin prided themselves on valor; Luqi fought each in turn and neither could prevail; both armies laid down weapons to watch.

units.zh: 晉已下魏博，梁將劉鄩軍於洹水，莊宗以百騎覘敵，遇鄩伏兵，圍之數重，幾不得脫，魯奇力戰，手殺百餘人，身被二十餘創，與莊宗決圍而出。
units.en: After Jin took Weibo, Liu Yan camped on the Huan; Zhuangzong scouted with a hundred horsemen, walked into an ambush, and was nearly trapped; Luqi fought hand to hand, slew a hundred men, took twenty wounds, and broke out with him.
units.literal: After Jin took Weibo, Liang’s Liu Yan camped on the Huan; Zhuangzong rode out with a hundred men to scout and met Yan’s ambush, encircled many times deep and nearly unable to escape; Luqi fought fiercely, killing more than a hundred with his own hand, taking twenty-odd wounds, and broke out with Zhuangzong.

units.zh: 莊宗益奇之，以為磁州刺史。
units.en: Zhuangzong prized him and made him prefect of Ci.
units.literal: Zhuangzong admired him all the more and made him prefect of Ci.

units.zh: 從戰中都，擒王彥章，莊宗壯之，賜絹千疋，拜鄭州防禦使。
units.en: At Zhongdu he captured Wang Yanzhang; Zhuangzong rewarded him with a thousand bolts of silk and made him Defender of Zhengzhou.
units.literal: In the campaign at Zhongdu he captured Wang Yanzhang; Zhuangzong praised him and granted a thousand bolts of silk, appointing him Defender of Zhengzhou.

units.zh: 遷河陽節度使，為政有惠愛。
units.en: He became governor of Heyang, ruling with kindness.
units.literal: He was transferred to military governor of Heyang, governing with kindness.

units.zh: 徙鎮忠武，河陽之人遮留不得行，父老詣京師乞留，明宗遣中使往諭之，魯奇乃得去。
units.en: Transferred to Zhongwu; Heyang’s people blocked his road; elders petitioned the capital; Mingzong sent an envoy to reason with them before Luqi could go.
units.literal: Moved to Zhongwu; the people of Heyang blocked his departure and would not let him go; elders went to the capital to beg he stay; Mingzong sent a palace envoy to explain, and only then could Luqi leave.

units.zh: 唐師伐荊南，以魯奇為招討副使，無功而還。
units.en: On Tang’s Jingnan campaign he served as deputy pacification commissioner and returned without success.
units.literal: When Tang campaigned against Jingnan, Luqi was deputy pacification commissioner; he returned without achievement.

units.zh: 徙鎮武信，東川董璋反，攻遂州，魯奇閉城拒之，旬月救兵不至，城中食盡，魯奇自刎死，年四十九。
units.en: Transferred to Wuxin; when Dong Zhang rebelled and attacked Suizhou, Luqi held the city; relief failed for ten days; food ran out; he killed himself at forty-nine.
units.literal: Transferred to Wuxin; Dong Zhang of Dongchuan rebelled and attacked Suizhou; Luqi shut the city and resisted; for ten days no relief came; food ran out; Luqi cut his throat and died, aged forty-nine.

units.zh: 吳巒兵猶可戰而不戰，魯奇食盡力窮而死，故取捨異。
units.en: Wu Luan’s men could still fight but would not; Luqi died when food and strength were gone—hence the difference in treatment.
units.literal: Wu Luan’s troops could still fight yet did not; Luqi died when food ran out and his strength was spent—hence the difference in how they are treated.

units.zh: 姚洪，本梁之小校也。
units.en: Yao Hong had been a petty officer of Liang.
units.literal: Yao Hong was originally a petty officer of Liang.

units.zh: 自董璋為梁將，洪嘗事璋，後事唐為指揮使。
units.en: He had served Dong Zhang when Zhang was a Liang general; later he served Tang as a commander.
units.literal: When Dong Zhang was a Liang general Hong had served him; later he served Tang as a commander.

units.zh: 長興中，遣洪將千人戍閬州。
units.en: In the Changxing era he garrisoned Langzhou with a thousand men.
units.literal: In the Changxing era he was sent with a thousand men to garrison Langzhou.

units.zh: 董璋反，遣人以書招洪，洪得璋書，輒投廁中。
units.en: When Zhang rebelled he sent letters to win Hong over; Hong threw each into the privy.
units.literal: When Dong Zhang rebelled he sent men with letters to win Hong; Hong, receiving Zhang’s letter, at once threw it into the privy.

units.zh: 後璋兵攻破閬州，執洪，璋曰：「爾為健兒，我遇汝厚，奈何負我邪？」
units.en: Zhang’s troops later took Langzhou and seized Hong; Zhang said, “You were a brave man—I favored you; how could you betray me?"
units.literal: Later Zhang’s troops took Langzhou and seized Hong; Zhang said, “You were a brave soldier—I treated you generously; how could you betray me?"

units.zh: 洪罵曰：「老賊！
units.en: Hong cursed, “Old bandit!
units.literal: Hong cursed: “Old bandit!

units.zh: 爾昔為李七郎奴，掃馬糞，得一臠殘炙，感恩不已。
units.en: You were once Seventh Master Li’s slave, shoveling dung, grateful forever for a scrap of meat.
units.literal: You were once slave to Seventh Master Li, sweeping horse dung, and were endlessly grateful for a scrap of leftover meat.

units.zh: 今天子用爾為節度使，何苦反邪？
units.en: The Son of Heaven made you a governor—why rebel?
units.literal: Now the Son of Heaven made you a military governor—why rebel?

units.zh: 吾能為國家死，不能從人奴以生！」
units.en: I can die for the state—I will not live as someone’s slave!”
units.literal: I can die for the state—I will not live as another man’s slave!”

units.zh: 璋怒，然鑊於前，令壯士十人刲其肉而食，洪至死大罵。
units.en: Zhang in rage set a cauldron boiling and had ten men slice his flesh and eat it; Hong cursed to the last.
units.literal: Zhang in rage set a cauldron before him and had ten strong men slice his flesh and eat it; Hong cursed to the end.

units.zh: 明宗聞之泣下，錄其二子，而厚卹其家。
units.en: Mingzong wept when he heard; he enrolled Hong’s two sons and richly comforted the family.
units.literal: When Mingzong heard he wept; he enrolled Hong’s two sons and richly comforted the family.

units.zh: 王思同
units.en: Wang Sitong
units.literal: Wang Sitong

units.zh: 王思同，幽州人也。
units.en: Wang Sitong was from Youzhou.
units.literal: Wang Sitong was a man of Youzhou.

units.zh: 其父敬柔，娶劉仁恭女，生思同。
units.en: His father Jingrou married Liu Rengong’s daughter and fathered Sitong.
units.literal: His father Jingrou married a daughter of Liu Rengong and fathered Sitong.

units.zh: 思同事仁恭為銀胡錄指揮使，仁恭為其子守光所囚，思同奔晉，以為飛勝指揮使。
units.en: Sitong served Rengong as Silver Hu Record commander; when Shouguang imprisoned his father, Sitong fled to Jin as commander of the Flying Victory Army.
units.literal: Sitong served Rengong as commander of the Silver Hu Record; Rengong was imprisoned by his son Shouguang; Sitong fled to Jin and was made commander of the Flying Victory Army.

units.zh: 梁、晉相距於莘，遣思同築壘楊劉，以功遷神武十軍都指揮使，累遷鄭州防禦使。
units.en: When Liang and Jin faced off at Xin he built fortifications at Yangliu; for merit he rose to commander of the Ten Divine Martial Armies and Defender of Zhengzhou.
units.literal: With Liang and Jin facing each other at Xin, he was sent to build fortifications at Yangliu; for merit he was made commander of the Ten Divine Martial Armies, rising to Defender of Zhengzhou.

units.zh: 思同為人敢勇，善騎射，好學，頗喜為詩，輕財重義，多禮文士，然未嘗有戰功。
units.en: Bold, skilled in archery, fond of study and poetry, generous and courteous to scholars—yet he never won a battle.
units.literal: Sitong was bold and brave, skilled in mounted archery, fond of study, and quite given to writing poetry; he was light with wealth and heavy on righteousness, courteous to literati—yet he never had battle merit.

units.zh: 明宗時，以久次為匡國軍節度使，徙鎮雄武。
units.en: Under Mingzong, after long service he governed Kuangguo, then Xiongwu.
units.literal: Under Mingzong, after long service he became military governor of Kuangguo, then moved to Xiongwu.

units.zh: 是時，吐蕃數為寇，而秦州無亭障，思同列四十餘柵以禦之。
units.en: Tibetans raided often; Qinzhou had no outposts; Sitong built forty-odd stockades.
units.literal: Tibetans raided often and Qinzhou had no outposts; Sitong set up more than forty stockades to guard against them.

units.zh: 居五年，來朝，明宗問以邊事，思同指畫山川，陳其利害。
units.en: After five years he came to court; Mingzong asked about the border; Sitong traced the mountains and explained every advantage and risk.
units.literal: After five years he came to court; Mingzong asked about the frontier; Sitong traced the mountains and rivers and laid out advantages and harms.

units.zh: 思同去，明宗顧左右曰：「人言思同不管事，能若是邪？」
units.en: As Sitong left, Mingzong told his attendants, “They say Sitong cannot govern—yet see this!"
units.literal: When Sitong left, Mingzong said to those around him, “Men say Sitong is no administrator—can he do such as this?"

units.zh: 於是始知其材，以為右武衛上將軍、京兆尹、西京留守。
units.en: Then he recognized Sitong’s ability and made him General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guard, metropolitan prefect, and western capital regent.
units.literal: Then he knew Sitong’s talent and made him General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guard, metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao, and western capital regent.

units.zh: 石敬瑭討董璋，思同為先鋒指揮使，兵入劍門，而後軍不繼，思同與璋戰，不勝而卻。
units.en: When Shi Jingtang attacked Dong Zhang, Sitong led the vanguard into Jianmen; the rear failed to follow; he fought Zhang, lost, and withdrew.
units.literal: When Shi Jingtang campaigned against Dong Zhang, Sitong was vanguard commander; the army entered Jianmen, but the rear did not follow; Sitong fought Zhang, could not win, and withdrew.

units.zh: 敬瑭兵罷，思同徙鎮山南西道，已而復為京兆尹、西京留守。
units.en: When Jingtang’s campaign ended, Sitong governed Shannan West Circuit, then again became metropolitan prefect and western capital regent.
units.literal: When Jingtang’s army was dismissed, Sitong was moved to govern Shannan West Circuit, then again became metropolitan prefect and western capital regent.

units.zh: 應順元年二月，潞王從珂反鳳翔，馳檄四鄰，言奸臣幸先帝疾病，賊殺秦王而立幼嗣，侵弱宗室，動搖藩方，陳己所以興兵討亂之狀。
units.en: In Yingshun’s first year, second month, Prince of Lu Congke rebelled at Fengxiang and circulated proclamations accusing treacherous ministers of murdering the Prince of Qin during the late emperor’s illness, enthroning a child, weakening the clan, and shaking the realm—and stating why he had taken arms.
units.literal: In the second month of the first year of Yingshun, Prince of Lu Congke rebelled at Fengxiang and sent proclamations to the four quarters, saying treacherous ministers had taken advantage of the late emperor’s illness to murder the Prince of Qin and set up a child heir, weakening the imperial clan and shaking the provinces, and stating why he had raised troops to punish disorder.

units.zh: 因遣伶奴安十十以五弦謁思同，欲因其歡以通意。
units.en: He sent the actor An Shishi with a five-string lute to visit Sitong, hoping pleasure would win him over.
units.literal: He sent the actor An Shishi with a five-string lute to visit Sitong, hoping to win him through pleasure.

units.zh: 是時，諸鎮皆懷向背，所得潞王書檄，雖以上聞，而不絕其使。
units.en: Every command wavered; they reported Congke’s letters to court yet kept his envoys coming.
units.literal: At that time every command wavered; though they reported the Prince of Lu’s letters upward, they did not cut off his envoys.

units.zh: 獨思同執十十及從珂所使推官郝詡等送京師。
units.en: Only Sitong seized Shishi and Congke’s staff officer Hao Xu and sent them to the capital.
units.literal: Only Sitong seized Shishi and Congke’s staff officer Hao Xu and the rest and sent them to the capital.

units.zh: 湣帝嘉其忠，即以思同為西面行營馬步軍都部署。
units.en: The Deposed Emperor praised his loyalty and made him overall western campaign commander.
units.literal: The Deposed Emperor praised his loyalty and at once made Sitong overall commander of horse and foot for the western campaign.

units.zh: 三月，會諸鎮兵圍鳳翔，破東西關城。
units.en: In the third month allied commands besieged Fengxiang and took the east and west gate cities.
units.literal: In the third month the commands united to besiege Fengxiang and broke the eastern and western gate cities.

units.zh: 從珂兵弱而守甚堅，外兵傷死者眾，從珂登城呼外兵而泣曰：「吾從先帝二十年，大小數百戰，甲不解體，金瘡滿身，士卒固嘗從我矣。
units.en: Congke was weak but held firm; besiegers died in droves; he mounted the wall weeping: “Twenty years I followed the late emperor, hundreds of battles, armor never off, scars over my body—you marched with me!
units.literal: Congke’s force was weak but his defense staunch; outside troops died in great numbers; Congke mounted the wall and called to the outside army in tears: “I followed the late emperor twenty years, fought hundreds of battles great and small, never doffed my armor, my body covered in scars—soldiers, you have marched with me!

units.zh: 今先帝新棄天下，而朝廷信用奸人，離間骨肉，我實何罪而見伐乎？」
units.en: The late emperor has just died, and the court’s wicked men sunder kin—what crime is mine that you attack me?"
units.literal: The late emperor has just left the world, and the court trusts wicked men who sunder flesh and blood—what crime is mine that I should be attacked?"

units.zh: 因慟哭。
units.en: Then he sobbed aloud.
units.literal: Then he wailed bitterly.

units.zh: 士卒聞者，皆悲憐之。
units.en: The soldiers who heard were moved to pity.
units.literal: Soldiers who heard were all moved to pity.

units.zh: 興元張虔釗攻城西，督戰甚急，士卒苦之，反兵攻虔釗，虔釗走。
units.en: Zhang Qianzhao of Xingyuan stormed the west wall so hard the men mutinied and drove him off.
units.literal: Zhang Qianzhao of Xingyuan assaulted the west of the city and pressed the fight fiercely; the troops suffered and turned on Qianzhao, who fled.

units.zh: 羽林指揮使楊思權呼曰：「潞王，吾主也！」
units.en: Yulin commander Yang Siquan shouted, “The Prince of Lu is our lord!"
units.literal: Yulin commander Yang Siquan shouted, “The Prince of Lu is our lord!"

units.zh: 乃引軍自西門入降從珂。
units.en: He led his men through the west gate to surrender to Congke.
units.literal: He then led his troops in through the west gate to surrender to Congke.

units.zh: 而思同未知，猶督戰。
units.en: Sitong had not yet heard, yet still pressed the attack.
units.literal: Sitong did not yet know, but still urged the fight on.

units.zh: 嚴衛指揮使尹暉麾其眾曰：「城西軍入城受賞矣！
units.en: Yanwei commander Yin Hui called to his men, “The western army is in the city taking rewards!
units.literal: Yanwei commander Yin Hui waved his troops and said, “The western army has entered the city for rewards!

units.zh: 何用戰邪？」
units.en: Why fight?"
units.literal: Why fight?"

units.zh: 士卒解甲棄仗，聲聞數里，遂皆入城降。
units.en: Men threw off armor; the clamor carried for li; all entered the city and surrendered.
units.literal: Soldiers cast off armor and weapons; the sound carried for li; then all entered the city and surrendered.

units.zh: 諸鎮之兵皆潰。
units.en: Every allied army broke and fled.
units.literal: The armies of every command broke and fled.

units.zh: 思同挺身走，至長安，西京副留守劉遂雍閉門不納，乃走潼關。
units.en: Sitong fled to Chang’an; Deputy Regent Liu Suiyong shut the gates; he fled toward Tong Pass.
units.literal: Sitong fled alone to Chang’an; Liu Suiyong, deputy regent of the western capital, shut the gates and would not admit him, and he fled toward Tong Pass.

units.zh: 從珂引兵東，至昭應，前鋒追執思同。
units.en: Congke marched east; at Zhaoying his vanguard captured Sitong.
units.literal: Congke marched east; at Zhaoying his vanguard overtook and seized Sitong.

units.zh: 從珂責曰：「罪可逃乎？」
units.en: Congke reproached him: “Did you think your crime could escape?"
units.literal: Congke reproached him: “Could your crime escape?"

units.zh: 思同曰：「非不知從王而得生，恐終死不能見先帝於地下。」
units.en: Sitong said, “I knew following you meant life—but I feared I could never face the late emperor in the grave.”
units.literal: Sitong said, “It is not that I did not know following the prince would let me live—I feared that in the end I could not face the late emperor underground.”

units.zh: 從珂愧其言，乃殺之。
units.en: Congke was shamed by his words and had him killed.
units.literal: Congke was shamed by his words and killed him.

units.zh: 漢高祖即位，贈侍中。
units.en: When Gaozu of Han took the throne, Sitong was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
units.literal: When Gaozu of Han took the throne, Sitong was posthumously made Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 思同東走，將自歸于天子，與元行欽走異，故予其死。
units.en: Sitong fled east to surrender to the emperor himself—unlike Yuan Xingqin’s flight—so he is counted among the martyrs.
units.literal: Sitong fled east intending to surrender himself to the Son of Heaven—unlike Yuan Xingqin’s flight—hence he is granted inclusion among those who died for the cause.

units.zh: 張敬達
units.en: Zhang Jingda
units.literal: Zhang Jingda

units.zh: 張敬達，字志通，代州人也，小字生鐵。
units.en: Zhang Jingda, courtesy name Zhitong, was from Daizhou; his childhood name was Raw Iron.
units.literal: Zhang Jingda, courtesy name Zhitong, was a man of Daizhou; his childhood name was Raw Iron.

units.zh: 少以騎射事唐莊宗為廳直軍使。
units.en: Young and skilled in archery, he served Zhuangzong as commissioner of the Hall Direct Army.
units.literal: In youth, skilled in mounted archery, he served Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang as commissioner of the Hall Direct Army.

units.zh: 明宗時，為河東馬步軍都指揮使，領欽州刺史，累遷彰國、大同軍節度使，徙鎮武信、晉昌。
units.en: Under Mingzong he commanded Hedong horse and foot and governed Qin, rose to governor of Zhangguo and Datong, then Wuxin and Jinchang.
units.literal: Under Mingzong he was overall commander of horse and foot in Hedong and prefect of Qin, rising to military governor of Zhangguo and Datong, then moved to Wuxin and Jinchang.

units.zh: 清泰二年，契丹數犯邊，廢帝以河東節度使石敬瑭兼大同、彰國、振武、威塞等軍蕃漢馬步軍都總管，屯於忻州，屯兵聚噪遮敬瑭呼「萬歲」，敬瑭斬三十餘人以止之。
units.en: In Qingtai’s second year Khitan raids multiplied; the Deposed Emperor made Shi Jingtang overall commander of the northern armies at Xinzhou; his troops mutinied, blocked him, and shouted “Long live!”; he beheaded thirty men to quell them.
units.literal: In the second year of Qingtai the Khitans raided the border repeatedly; the Deposed Emperor made Hedong governor Shi Jingtang overall commander of Tangut and Han horse and foot of Datong, Zhangguo, Zhenwu, Weisai, and other armies, camped at Xinzhou; the camp mutinied, blocked Jingtang, and shouted “Long live!”; Jingtang beheaded more than thirty to stop it.

units.zh: 廢帝疑敬瑭有異志，乃以敬達為北面副總管，以分其兵。
units.en: The Deposed Emperor suspected Jingtang and made Jingda deputy northern commander to split his force.
units.literal: The Deposed Emperor suspected Jingtang of disloyalty and made Jingda deputy northern commander to divide his troops.

units.zh: 明年夏，徙敬瑭鎮天平，遂以敬達為大同、彰國、振武、威塞等軍蕃漢馬步軍都部署，敬瑭因此遂反。
units.en: Next summer Jingtang was moved to Tianping; Jingda took his armies—and Jingtang rebelled.
units.literal: The next summer Jingtang was moved to govern Tianping, and Jingda was made overall commander of those armies; Jingtang therefore rebelled.

units.zh: 即以敬達為太原四面招討使。
units.en: Jingda was at once made four-sided pacification commissioner of Taiyuan.
units.literal: Jingda was at once made four-sided pacification commissioner of Taiyuan.

units.zh: 六月，兵圍太原，敬達為長城連柵，雲梯飛炮以攻之，所為城柵將成，輒有大風雨水暴至以壞之。
units.en: In the sixth month he besieged Taiyuan with linked ramparts, ladders, and catapults—yet whenever the works neared completion, storms smashed them.
units.literal: In the sixth month troops besieged Taiyuan; Jingda built linked ramparts and stormed with scaling ladders and flying catapults; whenever the works were nearly done, great winds and rain would burst forth and destroy them.

units.zh: 敬瑭求救於契丹。
units.en: Jingtang sought Khitan aid.
units.literal: Jingtang sought rescue from the Khitans.

units.zh: 九月，契丹耶律德光自雁門入，旌旗相屬五十餘里。
units.en: In the ninth month Yelü Deguang entered through Yanmen; his banners stretched fifty li.
units.literal: In the ninth month Yelü Deguang of the Khitans entered through Yanmen; banners and flags stretched more than fifty li.

units.zh: 德光先遣人告敬瑭曰：「吾欲今日破敵可乎？」
units.en: Deguang first asked Jingtang, “Shall I break the enemy today?"
units.literal: Deguang first sent word to Jingtang: “Shall I break the enemy today?"

units.zh: 敬瑭報曰：「大兵遠來，而賊勢方盛，要在成功，不必速也。」
units.en: Jingtang replied, “You have marched far; the foe is strong—success matters, not haste.”
units.literal: Jingtang replied: “Your great army has come far, and the foe’s power is at its height—the point is success, not speed.”

units.zh: 使者未復命，而兵已交。
units.en: Before the envoy returned, battle had begun.
units.literal: Before the envoy could return, the armies had already joined battle.

units.zh: 敬達陣於西山，契丹以羸騎三千，革鞭木鐙，人馬皆不甲胄，以趨唐軍。
units.en: Jingda formed on the western hills; the Khitans sent three thousand unarmored horses with leather whips and wooden stirrups to charge the Tang line.
units.literal: Jingda formed battle on the western hills; the Khitans sent three thousand weak horses with leather whips and wooden stirrups, men and horses all without armor, charging the Tang army.

units.zh: 唐軍爭馳之，契丹兵走。
units.en: The Tang army gave chase; the Khitans fled.
units.literal: The Tang army raced after them; the Khitan troops fled.

units.zh: 追至汾曲，伏發，斷唐軍為二，其在北者皆死，死者萬餘人。
units.en: At Fen Qu an ambush sprang; the Tang line was cut in two; everyone north of the trap died—more than ten thousand.
units.literal: Pursuit reached Fen Qu; ambush sprang; the Tang army was cut in two; all in the north died—more than ten thousand dead.

units.zh: 敬達收軍柵晉安，契丹圍之。
units.en: Jingda fell back to Jin’an; the Khitans besieged him.
units.literal: Jingda gathered his troops and fortified at Jin’an; the Khitans besieged them.

units.zh: 廢帝遣趙延壽、範延光等救之。
units.en: The Deposed Emperor sent Zhao Yanshou, Fan Yanguang, and others to relieve him.
units.literal: The Deposed Emperor sent Zhao Yanshou, Fan Yanguang, and others to rescue him.

units.zh: 延壽屯團柏谷，延光屯遼州，相去皆百餘里。
units.en: Yanshou camped at Tuanbai Valley, Yanguang at Liaozhou—more than a hundred li apart.
units.literal: Yanshou camped at Tuanbai Valley, Yanguang at Liaozhou—each more than a hundred li away.

units.zh: 契丹兵圍敬達者，自晉安寨南，長百餘里，闊五十里，敬達軍中望之，但見穹廬連屬如岡阜，四面亙以毛索，掛鈴為警，縱犬往來。
units.en: The Khitan ring around Jin’an ran a hundred li south of the stockade and fifty li wide; inside Jingda’s camp yurts rose like hills; raw ropes and bells guarded every side; dogs patrolled the lines.
units.literal: The Khitans surrounding Jingda stretched from south of the Jin’an stockade for more than a hundred li, fifty li wide; in Jingda’s camp one saw only yurts linked like hillocks; on four sides they ran raw ropes, hung bells for alarm, and let dogs run to and fro.

units.zh: 敬達軍中有夜出者，輒為契丹所得，由是閉壁不敢復出。
units.en: Night sorties from Jingda’s camp were captured; thereafter the walls stayed shut.
units.literal: Anyone who went out by night from Jingda’s army was taken by the Khitans; thereafter they shut the walls and dared not go out again.

units.zh: 延壽等皆有二心，無救敬達意。
units.en: Yanshou and the rest were half-hearted and had no will to save him.
units.literal: Yanshou and the rest all had divided hearts and no will to save Jingda.

units.zh: 敬達猶有兵五萬人、馬萬匹，久之食盡，削木篩糞以飼其馬，馬死者食之，已而馬盡。
units.en: Jingda still had fifty thousand men and ten thousand horses; food ran out; they shaved wood and sifted dung for the horses, then ate the dead horses—until there were no horses left.
units.literal: Jingda still had fifty thousand men and ten thousand horses; in time food ran out; they shaved wood and sifted dung to feed the horses; when horses died they ate them; soon the horses were gone.

units.zh: 副招討使楊光遠勸敬達降晉，敬達自以不忍背唐，而救兵且至，光遠促之不已，敬達曰：「諸公何相迫邪！
units.en: Deputy commissioner Yang Guangyuan urged surrender to Jin; Jingda could not betray Tang and believed relief was near; Guangyuan pressed him; Jingda said, “Why do you hound me so!
units.literal: Deputy pacification commissioner Yang Guangyuan urged Jingda to surrender to Jin; Jingda himself could not bear to betray Tang, and relief was due; Guangyuan pressed without cease; Jingda said, “Gentlemen, why do you press me so!

units.zh: 何不殺我而降？」
units.en: Why not kill me and surrender?"
units.literal: Why not kill me and surrender?"

units.zh: 光遠即斬敬達降。
units.en: Guangyuan beheaded Jingda and surrendered.
units.literal: Guangyuan at once beheaded Jingda and surrendered.

units.zh: 契丹耶律德光聞敬達死，哀其忠，遣人收葬之。
units.en: Deguang mourned Jingda’s loyalty and sent men to bury him.
units.literal: When Yelü Deguang heard Jingda was dead he mourned his loyalty and sent men to gather and bury him.

units.zh: 而傳錄其死者，終嘉其不降也。
units.en: Yet the biography records the dead man and ultimately honors him for refusing to submit.
units.literal: Yet the biography records the dead man and ultimately praises him for not submitting.

units.zh: 然己雖不屈而諷人降賊，故不得為死節。
units.en: Yet though he himself did not yield, he urged others to surrender to the rebels, so he did not qualify as a martyr of integrity.
units.literal: However, though he himself did not yield, he urged others to surrender to the rebels; therefore he did not qualify as one who died for integrity.

units.zh: 翟進宗
units.en: Di Jinzong
units.literal: Di Jinzong

units.zh: 〈（張萬迪附）〉
units.en: (Zhang Wandi appended)
units.literal: (Zhang Wandi appended)

units.zh: 翟進宗、張萬迪者，皆不知其何人也。
units.en: Di Jinzong and Zhang Wandi—both origins unknown.
units.literal: Di Jinzong and Zhang Wandi—their origins are unknown.

units.zh: 初皆事唐，後事晉，進宗為淄州刺史，萬迪為登州刺史。
units.en: Both served Tang, then Jin; Jinzong governed Zi, Wandi Deng.
units.literal: Both first served Tang, then Jin; Jinzong was prefect of Zi, Wandi prefect of Deng.

units.zh: 楊光遠反，以騎兵數百脅取二刺史至青州，萬迪聽命，而進宗獨不屈，光遠遂殺進宗。
units.en: When Yang Guangyuan rebelled he seized both prefects with cavalry; Wandi submitted, Jinzong alone refused; Guangyuan killed Jinzong.
units.literal: When Yang Guangyuan rebelled he sent several hundred horsemen to seize the two prefects and bring them to Qingzhou; Wandi obeyed, but Jinzong alone would not yield; Guangyuan therefore killed Jinzong.

units.zh: 出帝贈進宗左武衛上將軍。
units.en: The Chu Emperor of Later Jin posthumously made Jinzong General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard.
units.literal: The Chu Emperor of Later Jin posthumously made Jinzong General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard.

units.zh: 及光遠平，曲赦青州，雖光遠子孫皆見慰釋，而獨不赦萬迪，暴其罪而斬之。
units.en: When Guangyuan fell, Qingzhou was amnestied—even his kin were freed—yet Wandi alone was denied pardon, his crimes proclaimed, and he was beheaded.
units.literal: When Guangyuan was pacified, Qingzhou was pardoned in a special amnesty—even Guangyuan’s descendants were comforted and released—yet Wandi alone was not pardoned; his crimes were proclaimed and he was beheaded.

units.zh: 詔求進宗屍，加禮歸葬，葬事官給，以其子仁欽為東頭供奉官。
units.en: The court sought Jinzong’s body, buried him at state expense, and made his son Renqin an Eastern Head Palace Attendant.
units.literal: An edict sought Jinzong’s corpse; he was buried with full rites at state expense; his son Renqin was made an Eastern Head Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 沈斌字安時，徐州下邳人也。
units.en: Shen Bin, courtesy name Anshi, was from Xiapi in Xuzhou.
units.literal: Shen Bin, courtesy name Anshi, was a man of Xiapi in Xuzhou.

units.zh: 少為軍卒，事梁為拱辰都指揮使。
units.en: In youth he was a soldier; under Liang he became commander of the Gongchen Guard.
units.literal: In youth he was a soldier; serving Liang he became commander of the Gongchen Guard.

units.zh: 後事唐，從魏王繼岌破蜀，平康延孝，以功為虢州刺史，歷隨、趙等八州刺史。
units.en: Later he served Tang, followed Prince Jiji in the Shu campaign and pacification of Kang Yanxiao, and for merit became prefect of Guo, then held eight prefectures including Sui and Zhao.
units.literal: Later he served Tang, followed Prince of Wei Jiji in conquering Shu and pacifying Kang Yanxiao, and for merit became prefect of Guo, then served in turn as prefect of eight prefectures including Sui and Zhao.

units.zh: 晉開運元年，為祁州刺史。
units.en: In Jin’s first Kaiyun year he became prefect of Qi.
units.literal: In the first year of Kaiyun of Jin he became prefect of Qi.

units.zh: 契丹犯塞至于榆林，過祁州，斌以謂契丹深入晉地而歸兵羸乏可擊，即以州兵邀之。
units.en: When the Khitans raided to Yulin and passed Qi, Bin judged their return column deep in Jin territory was weary and vulnerable, and intercepted them with prefectural troops.
units.literal: When the Khitans raided the frontier as far as Yulin and passed Qi Prefecture, Bin judged that the Khitans, deep in Jin territory on their return with weary troops, could be struck, and intercepted them with the prefectural army.

units.zh: 契丹以精騎剗門，斌兵多死，城中無備，虜將趙延壽留兵急攻之，延壽招斌降，斌從城上罵延壽曰：「公父子誤計，陷于腥膻，忍以犬羊之眾，殘賊父母之邦，斌能為國死爾，不能效公所為也！」
units.en: Khitans sent elite cavalry to storm the gate; Bin lost many men and the city was unprepared. Zhao Yanshou pressed the assault and called on Bin to surrender. From the wall Bin cursed him: “You and your father chose wrongly and fell among barbarians—how can you use a herd of dogs and sheep to ravage your own homeland? I can die for the state, but I will never do as you have done!”
units.literal: The Khitans sent elite cavalry to break the gate; many of Bin’s men died; the city was unprepared; the barbarian general Zhao Yanshou left troops to press the assault, called on Bin to surrender, and Bin cursed Yanshou from the wall: “You and your father chose wrongly and fell among stinking barbarians—how can you bear to use a flock of dogs and sheep to ravage your own parents’ land? Bin can die for the state, but he cannot imitate what you have done!”

units.zh: 已而城陷，斌自盡，其家屬皆沒于虜。
units.en: Soon the city fell; Bin killed himself, and his family were all taken captive.
units.literal: Soon the city fell; Bin killed himself, and his household were all taken by the barbarians.

units.zh: 王清，字去瑕，洺州曲周人也。
units.en: Wang Qing, courtesy name Quxia, was from Quzhou in Luozhou.
units.literal: Wang Qing, courtesy name Quxia, was a man of Quzhou in Luozhou.

units.zh: 初事唐為寧衛指揮使。
units.en: He first served Tang as commander of the Ningwei Guard.
units.literal: He first served Tang as commander of the Ningwei Guard.

units.zh: 後事晉為奉國都虞候。
units.en: Later he served Jin as chief adjutant of the Fengguo Army.
units.literal: Later he served Jin as chief adjutant of the Fengguo Army.

units.zh: 安從進叛襄州，從高行周攻之，逾年不能下，清謂行周曰：「從進閉孤城以自守，其勢豈得久邪？」
units.en: When An Congjin rebelled at Xiangzhou, Gao Xingzhou besieged him a year without success; Qing said, “He holds one city—how long can that last?"
units.literal: When An Congjin rebelled at Xiangzhou, Gao Xingzhou besieged him more than a year without taking the city; Qing said to Xingzhou, “Congjin holds a lone city—how long can he last?"

units.zh: 因請先登，遂攻破之。
units.en: He asked to lead the assault and took the city.
units.literal: He asked to lead the assault and broke the city.

units.zh: 開運二年冬，從杜重威戰陽城，清以力戰功為步軍之最，加檢校司徒。
units.en: In Kaiyun’s second winter he fought with Du Chongwei at Yangcheng; for valor he was judged best among the infantry and made Acting Minister of Works.
units.literal: In the winter of the second year of Kaiyun he followed Du Chongwei at the battle of Yangcheng; for fierce fighting he was judged foremost among the infantry and made Acting Minister of Works.

units.zh: 是冬，重威軍中渡橋南，虜軍其北以相拒，而虜以精騎並西山出晉軍後，南擊欒城，斷晉餉道。
units.en: That winter Chongwei camped south of Zhongdu Bridge, the Khitans north; Khitan elite cavalry swept behind the Jin line along the western hills, struck Luancheng, and cut Jin’s supplies.
units.literal: That winter Chongwei’s army was south of the Zhongdu Bridge and the barbarians north, facing each other; the barbarians sent elite cavalry along the western hills behind the Jin army and struck south at Luancheng, cutting Jin’s supply route.

units.zh: 清謂重威曰：「晉軍危矣！
units.en: Qing told Chongwei, “The Jin army is doomed!
units.literal: Qing said to Chongwei, “The Jin army is in peril!

units.zh: 今去鎮州五里，而守死於此，營孤食盡，將若之何？
units.en: Zhenzhou is five li away, yet we sit here to die, cut off and starving—what now?
units.literal: Zhenzhou is only five li away, yet we sit here waiting to die, camp isolated and food gone—what is to be done?

units.zh: 請以步兵二千為先鋒，奪橋開路，公率諸軍繼進以入鎮州，可以守也。」
units.en: Give me two thousand foot to seize the bridge; you follow with the main army into Zhenzhou—we can hold."
units.literal: Let me take two thousand foot as vanguard, seize the bridge and open the road; you lead the main army after and enter Zhenzhou—we can hold it."

units.zh: 重威許之，遣與宋彥筠俱前，清與虜戰，敗之，奪其橋。
units.en: Chongwei agreed and sent him with Song Yanyun; Qing beat the Khitans and took the bridge.
units.literal: Chongwei agreed and sent him forward with Song Yanyun; Qing fought the barbarians, defeated them, and took the bridge.

units.zh: 是時，重威已有二誌，猶豫不肯進，彥筠亦退走，清曰：「吾獨死於此矣！」
units.en: Chongwei already wavered and would not advance; Yanyun retreated; Qing said, “Then I die here alone!"
units.literal: By then Chongwei already had two minds and hesitated to advance; Yanyun also retreated; Qing said, “I die here alone!"

units.zh: 因力戰而死。
units.en: He fought on and died.
units.literal: He fought on with all his strength and died.

units.zh: 年五十三。
units.en: He was fifty-three.
units.literal: He was fifty-three.

units.zh: 漢高祖立，贈清太傅。
units.en: When Gaozu of Han took the throne, Qing was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: When Gaozu of Han took the throne, Qing was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 史彥超
units.en: Shi Yanchao
units.literal: Shi Yanchao

units.zh: 史彥超，雲州人也。
units.en: Shi Yanchao was from Yunzhou.
units.literal: Shi Yanchao was a man of Yunzhou.

units.zh: 為人勇悍驍捷。
units.en: He was fierce, hardy, and swift.
units.literal: As a man he was fierce, hardy, and swift.

units.zh: 周太祖起魏時，彥超為漢龍捷都指揮使，以兵從。
units.en: When Taizu of Zhou rose in Wei, Yanchao commanded the Han Dragon Swift Army and marched with him.
units.literal: When Taizu of Zhou rose in Wei, Yanchao was commander of the Han Dragon Swift Army and marched with him.

units.zh: 太祖入立，遷虎捷都指揮使，戍於晉州。
units.en: When Taizu took the throne, Yanchao commanded the Tiger Swift Army and garrisoned Jinzhou.
units.literal: When Taizu took the throne, Yanchao was made commander of the Tiger Swift Army and garrisoned at Jinzhou.

units.zh: 劉旻攻晉州，州無主帥，知州王萬敢不能拒，彥超以戍兵堅守月餘，太祖遣王峻救之，旻兵解去。
units.en: Liu Min attacked Jinzhou; there was no commander; Prefect Wang Wangan could not hold; Yanchao held a month until Wang Jun relieved him and Min withdrew.
units.literal: Liu Min attacked Jinzhou; the prefecture had no chief commander; Prefect Wang Wangan could not resist; Yanchao held firm with the garrison for more than a month; Taizu sent Wang Jun to relieve him, and Min’s army withdrew.

units.zh: 以功遷龍捷右廂都指揮使，領鄭州防禦使。
units.en: For merit he became commander of the Dragon Swift right wing and Defender of Zhengzhou.
units.literal: For merit he was made commander of the Right Wing of the Dragon Swift Army and Defender of Zhengzhou.

units.zh: 周、漢戰高平，彥超為前鋒，先登陷陣，以功拜感德軍節度使。
units.en: At Gaoping he led the vanguard, first over the wall; for merit he became governor of Gande.
units.literal: At the Zhou–Han battle of Gaoping, Yanchao was vanguard, first to scale and break the line; for merit he was made military governor of Gande.

units.zh: 周兵圍漢太原，契丹救漢，出忻、代。
units.en: When Zhou besieged Han’s Taiyuan, Khitans came from Xin and Dai to aid Han.
units.literal: When Zhou besieged Taiyuan of Han, the Khitans came to aid Han from Xin and Dai.

units.zh: 世宗遣符彥卿拒之，以彥超為先鋒，戰忻口，彥超勇憤俱發，左右馳擊，解而復合者數四，遂歿於陣。
units.en: Shizong sent Fu Yanqing to meet them with Yanchao as vanguard; at Xin Pass Yanchao charged four times through the line and fell.
units.literal: Shizong sent Fu Yanqing to meet them and made Yanchao vanguard; at Xin Pass Yanchao fought with courage and rage, charging left and right; he broke through and re-formed four times, then fell in the line.

units.zh: 是時，世宗敗漢高平，乘勝而進，圍城之役，諸將議不一，故久無成功。
units.en: Shizong had won at Gaoping and pressed on, but at the siege the generals quarrelled and success was slow.
units.literal: At that time Shizong had defeated Han at Gaoping and pressed on in victory; in the siege campaign the generals could not agree, and so for long there was no success.

units.zh: 世宗欲解去而未決，聞彥超戰死，遽班師，倉卒之際，亡失甚眾。
units.en: Shizong wanted to withdraw but hesitated; hearing Yanchao had fallen, he withdrew at once—in the haste losses were heavy.
units.literal: Shizong wished to withdraw but had not decided; when he heard Yanchao had died in battle he at once withdrew the army; in the haste the losses were very great.

units.zh: 世宗既惜彥超而憤無成功，憂忿不食者數日。
units.en: Shizong grieved Yanchao and raged at failure; for days he would not eat.
units.literal: Shizong both grieved Yanchao and raged at failure; for several days he ate nothing in anger and sorrow.

units.zh: 贈彥超太師，優恤其家焉。
units.en: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor; his family was richly comforted.
units.literal: Yanchao was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and his family richly comforted.

units.zh: 孫晟，初名鳳，又名忌，密州人也。
units.en: Sun Cheng—born Feng, also called Ji—was from Mizhou.
units.literal: Sun Cheng—his original name was Feng, also called Ji—was a man of Mizhou.

units.zh: 好學，有文辭，尤長於詩。
units.en: He loved learning, wrote well, and excelled at poetry.
units.literal: Fond of study, he had literary skill and was especially good at poetry.

units.zh: 少為道士，居廬山簡寂宮。
units.en: In youth he was a Daoist at Jianji Palace on Mount Lu.
units.literal: In youth he was a Daoist priest at Jianji Palace on Mount Lu.

units.zh: 常畫唐詩人賈島像置於屋壁，晨夕事之。
units.en: He painted the Tang poet Jia Dao and hung the portrait on his wall, honoring it morning and evening.
units.literal: He often painted a portrait of the Tang poet Jia Dao and set it on the wall, serving it morning and evening.

units.zh: 簡寂宮道士惡晟，以為妖，以杖驅出之。
units.en: The priests hated him as an occultist and drove him out with staves.
units.literal: The priests of Jianji Palace hated Cheng, took him for a sorcerer, and drove him out with staves.

units.zh: 乃儒服北之趙、魏，謁唐莊宗於鎮州，莊宗以晟為著作佐郎。
units.en: He donned scholar’s robes, went north to Zhao and Wei, and met Zhuangzong at Zhenzhou, who made him Assistant in the Palace Library.
units.literal: He then put on scholar’s dress and went north to Zhao and Wei, visiting Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang at Zhenzhou; Zhuangzong made him Assistant in the Palace Library.

units.zh: 天成中，朱守殷鎮汴州，辟為判官。
units.en: In the Tiancheng era Zhu Shouyin governed Bianzhou and made him administrative aide.
units.literal: In the Tiancheng era Zhu Shouyin governed Bianzhou and took Cheng as administrative aide.

units.zh: 守殷反，伏誅，晟乃棄其妻子，亡命陳、宋之間。
units.en: When Shouyin rebelled and was executed, Cheng abandoned wife and children and fled between Chen and Song.
units.literal: When Shouyin rebelled and was executed, Cheng abandoned wife and children and fled between Chen and Song.

units.zh: 安重誨惡晟，以謂教守殷反者晟也，畫其像購之，不可得，遂族其家。
units.en: An Chonghui blamed him for teaching Shouyin rebellion, posted his likeness for reward, could not catch him, and exterminated his family.
units.literal: An Chonghui hated Cheng, saying he had taught Shouyin to rebel; he painted his likeness and offered a reward, but could not catch him, and so exterminated his family.

units.zh: 晟奔於吳。
units.en: Cheng fled to Wu.
units.literal: Cheng fled to Wu.

units.zh: 是時，李方篡楊氏，多招四方之士，得晟，喜其文辭，使為教令，由是知名。
units.en: Li Fang seized power in Wu and gathered talent; he prized Cheng’s prose for edicts, and Cheng became famous.
units.literal: At that time Li Fang seized the Yang house and recruited men from all quarters; gaining Cheng, he delighted in his writing and had him draft edicts; thereby Cheng became known.

units.zh: 晟為人口吃，遇人不能道寒暄，已而坐定，談辯鋒生，聽者忘倦。
units.en: He stammered at greetings, yet once seated his talk blazed and listeners forgot fatigue.
units.literal: Cheng stammered and could not exchange greetings when he met people; but once seated, debate flashed forth and listeners forgot weariness.

units.zh: 尤愛之，引與計議，多合意，以為右僕射，與馮延巳並為相。
units.en: Li Jing loved him, consulted him often, made him Right Vice Director and chief minister with Feng Yansi.
units.literal: Jing loved him especially, drew him into counsel—often in accord—and made him Right Vice Director and chief minister alongside Feng Yansi.

units.zh: 晟輕延巳為人，常曰：「金碗玉杯而盛狗屎可乎？」
units.en: Cheng despised Yansi and said, “A golden bowl and jade cup full of dog shit—is that fitting?"
units.literal: Cheng looked down on Yansi’s character and often said, “A golden bowl and jade cup holding dog shit—can that be?"

units.zh: 晟事父子二十餘年，官至司空，家益富驕，每食不設几案，使眾妓各執一器，環立而侍，號「肉臺盤」，時人多效之。
units.en: Serving father and son twenty years, he rose to Minister of Works; his house grew rich and arrogant; at meals singing girls stood in a ring each holding a dish—the “Flesh Pedestal”—and many copied him.
units.literal: Cheng served father and son more than twenty years, rose to Minister of Works, and his household grew rich and proud; at each meal he set no tables but had a ring of singing girls each holding a vessel and waiting—called the “Flesh Pedestal”—and many imitated it.

units.zh: 周世宗征淮，李景懼，始遣泗州牙將王知朗至徐州，奉書以求和，世宗不答。
units.en: When Shizong campaigned on the Huai, Jing in fear sent Wang Zhilang to Xuzhou to sue for peace; Shizong ignored him.
units.literal: When Shizong of Zhou campaigned on the Huai, Jing feared and first sent Sizhou aide Wang Zhilang to Xuzhou with a letter seeking peace; Shizong did not answer.

units.zh: 又遣翰林學士鐘謨、文理院學士李德明奉表稱臣，不答。
units.en: He sent Zhong Mo and Li Deming with a memorial of submission; still no answer.
units.literal: He again sent Academician Zhong Mo and Institute scholar Li Deming with a memorial calling himself subject; no answer.

units.zh: 乃遣禮部尚書王崇質副晟奉表，謨與晟等皆言景願割壽、濠、泗、楚、光、海六州之地，歲貢百萬以佐軍。
units.en: Then he sent Minister of Rites Wang Chongzhi as deputy to Cheng with a memorial; Mo, Cheng, and the rest offered six Huai prefectures and a million a year in tribute.
units.literal: Then he sent Minister of Rites Wang Chongzhi as Cheng’s deputy with a memorial; Mo, Cheng, and the rest all said Jing would cede the six prefectures of Shou, Hao, Si, Chu, Guang, and Hai and pay a million a year to support the army.

units.zh: 而世宗已取滁、揚、濠、泗諸州，欲盡取淮南乃止，因留使者不遣，而攻壽州益急。
units.en: Shizong had already taken Chu, Yang, Hao, and Si and wanted all Huainan; he detained the envoys and tightened the siege of Shouzhou.
units.literal: But Shizong had already taken Chu, Yang, Hao, and Si and wished to take all Huainan before stopping; he detained the envoys and pressed the siege of Shouzhou harder.

units.zh: 謨等見世宗英武非景敵，而師甚盛，壽春且危，乃曰：「願陛下寬臣五日之誅，容臣還取景表，盡獻淮北諸州。」
units.en: Mo and the rest saw Shizong’s might and Shouchun’s peril; they said, “Grant us five days to return with Jing’s offer of all north Huai prefectures."
units.literal: Mo and the others saw that Jing was no match for Shizong's martial prowess, that the army was overwhelmingly strong, and that Shouchun was near peril; they said, “We beg Your Majesty to grant us five days' reprieve, so that we may return and bring Jing's memorial offering all the prefectures north of the Huai.”

units.zh: 世宗許之，遣供奉官安弘道押德明、崇質南還，而謨與晟皆見留。
units.en: Shizong agreed, sent An Hongdao south with Deming and Chongzhi, and kept Mo and Cheng.
units.literal: Shizong agreed and sent Palace Attendant An Hongdao to escort Deming and Chongzhi south, while Mo and Cheng were detained.

units.zh: 德明等既還，景悔，不肯割地。
units.en: When Deming returned, Jing repented and refused to cede land.
units.literal: When Deming and the rest returned, Jing repented and would not cede land.

units.zh: 世宗亦以暑雨班師，留李重進、張永德等分攻廬、壽，周兵所得揚、泰諸州，皆不能守，景兵復振。
units.en: Shizong withdrew for summer rain, leaving Chongjin and Yongde to attack Lu and Shou; Zhou lost Yang and Tai; Jing’s army revived.
units.literal: Shizong also withdrew for summer rains; he left Li Chongjin and Zhang Yongde to attack Lu and Shou separately; the Yang and Tai prefectures Zhou had taken could not be held; Jing’s army revived.

units.zh: 重進與永德兩軍相疑，有隙，永德上書言重進反，世宗不聽。
units.en: Chongjin and Yongde mistrusted each other; Yongde accused Chongjin of rebellion; Shizong disbelieved.
units.literal: Chongjin and Yongde distrusted each other and had a rift; Yongde memorialized that Chongjin had rebelled; Shizong did not believe it.

units.zh: 景知二將之相疑也，乃以蠟丸書遺重進，勸其反。
units.en: Jing knew they were at odds and sent Chongjin a wax-sealed letter urging rebellion.
units.literal: Jing knew the two generals were at odds and sent a wax-sealed letter urging Chongjin to rebel.

units.zh: 初，晟之奉使也，語崇質曰：「吾行必不免，然吾終不負永陵一抷土也。」
units.en: When Cheng first went as envoy he told Chongzhi, “I shall surely not return—but I will never betray Yongling’s soil."
units.literal: When Cheng first went on embassy he told Chongzhi, “My journey will surely not spare me—but I will never betray a handful of soil from Yongling."

units.zh: 永陵者，墓也。
units.en: Yongling means the royal tomb.
units.literal: Yongling means the tomb.

units.zh: 及崇質還，而晟與鐘謨俱至京師，館於都亭驛，待之甚厚，每朝會入閣，使班東省官後，召見必飲以醇酒。
units.en: When Chongzhi returned, Cheng and Mo reached the capital, lodged at the Capital Pavilion, were honored at court, ranked after eastern officials, and were plied with wine at every audience.
units.literal: When Chongzhi returned, Cheng and Zhong Mo both reached the capital and lodged at the Capital Pavilion; they were treated very generously; at each court session they ranked after the eastern-province officials; when summoned they were always given strong wine.

units.zh: 已而周兵數敗，盡失所得諸州，世宗憂之，召晟問江南事，晟不對，世宗怒，未有以發。
units.en: Soon Zhou armies lost repeatedly; Shizong worried and asked Cheng about the south; Cheng was silent; Shizong raged but had no cause.
units.literal: Before long Zhou armies suffered repeated defeats and lost all the prefectures they had taken; Shizong worried and summoned Cheng to ask about affairs south of the Yangzi; Cheng would not answer; Shizong grew angry but had no pretext.

units.zh: 會重進以景蠟丸書來上，多斥周過惡以為言，由是發怒曰：「晟來使我，言景畏吾神武，願得北面稱臣，保無二心，安得此指斥之言乎？」
units.en: When Chongjin sent up Jing’s wax letter full of Zhou’s crimes, Shizong exploded: “Cheng told me Jing feared my might and would submit—how is this abuse?"
units.literal: When Chongjin sent up Jing’s wax letter, full of Zhou’s faults and wickedness, Shizong flared: “Cheng came as my envoy and said Jing feared my divine might and wished to submit north and keep faith—how comes this abuse?"

units.zh: 亟召待衛軍虞候韓通收晟下獄，及其從者二百餘人皆殺之。
units.en: He summoned Han Tong, imprisoned Cheng, and killed him and two hundred followers.
units.literal: He at once summoned Guard Army commissioner Han Tong, seized Cheng and put him in prison, and killed him and more than two hundred followers.

units.zh: 晟臨死，世宗猶遣近臣問之，晟終不對，神色怡然，正其衣冠南望而拜曰：「臣惟以死報國爾！」
units.en: At execution Shizong still sent an attendant to question him; Cheng was calm, straightened his robes, bowed south, and said, “I repay the state with death alone!"
units.literal: At the point of death Shizong still sent a close attendant to question him; Cheng never answered, his expression calm; he straightened his robes, bowed south, and said, “I have only death to repay the state!"

units.zh: 乃就刑。
units.en: Then he was executed.
units.literal: Then he went to the block.

units.zh: 晟既死，鐘謨亦貶耀州司馬。
units.en: After Cheng died, Mo was demoted to military adjutant of Yao.
units.literal: After Cheng died, Zhong Mo was demoted to military adjutant of Yao.

units.zh: 其後，世宗怒解，憐晟忠，悔殺之，召拜鐘謨衛尉少卿。
units.en: Later Shizong’s anger cooled; he pitied Cheng and regretted the killing; he recalled Mo as Vice Director of the Imperial Guard.
units.literal: Later Shizong’s anger eased; he pitied Cheng’s loyalty and regretted killing him; he recalled and made Zhong Mo Vice Director of the Imperial Guard.

units.zh: 景已割江北，遂遣謨還，而景聞晟死，亦贈魯國公。
units.en: Jing had ceded land north of the Yangzi and sent Mo back; hearing Cheng was dead, he too posthumously made him Duke of Lu.
units.literal: Jing had already ceded north of the Yangzi and sent Mo back; when Jing heard Cheng was dead he too posthumously made him Duke of Lu.
